If you need the exact page in a printed KJV Bible, it’s usually found on page 359–360 (depending on the edition), or you can locate the verse in most modern Bible apps/search tools.

So, the direct source in the “book” for the quote is **Job chapter 19, verse 20**.

steps.text:
The expression **“by the skin of your teeth”** comes from the **Bible**—specifically from the Book of **Job** in the King‑James Version (KJV). 

**Verse:**  
- **Job 19:20 (KJV)** – *“I am nothing but skin and bones; I have escaped only by the skin of my teeth.”*

This is the original text in which the idiom appears; all other uses—including any quotation attributed to a figure named Mary—are later adaptations or paraphrases of this verse. If you need the exact page in a printed KJV Bible, it’s usually found on page 359–360 (depending on the edition), or you can locate the verse in most modern Bible apps/search tools.

So, the direct source in the “book” for the quote is **Job chapter 19, verse 20**.
